name: math_antipode_reversing

phase_0.boundary_condition: the algebraic closure of the Hopf structure

VINIT.justification: the raw substrate before the introduction of multiplication or co-multiplication

TANCH.justification: the terminal boundary that bounds the algebraic operations within the field

AFWD.justification: the forward transformation of an element within the algebra

AREV.justification: the contravariant map that reverses the orientation of the element

CLINK.justification: the sequential application of the antipode and the identity through the product

IMSCRIB.justification: the self-recognition of the element as its own reference point

FSPLIT.justification: the operation that maps an element into a tensor product of two components

FFUSE.justification: the operation that maps the tensor product back into a single element

EVALT.justification: the state where the transformation maintains the original parity

EVALF.justification: the state where the transformation flips the parity via the antipode

ENGAGR.justification: the state where the element exists in a superposition of orientations at the limit

IFIX.justification: the permanent record of the orientation state after the antipode application

phase_3.void_description: the null space before algebraic definition
phase_3.both_description: chiral asymmetry where both orientations are held in tension

steps.domain_action: initialize the base vector space for the element
identify the element as a distinct algebraic entity
apply co-multiplication to branch the element into a tensor pair
route the primary component through the identity morphism
apply the forward morphism to the identity branch
apply the antipode S to the secondary branch to reverse orientation
anchor the reversed orientation on the secondary branch
apply multiplication to the identity and antipode branches
compose the result into the convolution product
hold the resulting scalar value in the criticality fixed-point
record the final orientation state as a permanent topological invariant
close the operation within the terminal scalar boundary

phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: the order of operations in the convolution formula

phase_6.cycle_cost: computational overhead of the antipode inversion
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the antipode is an anti-automorphism that preserves the structural information of the algebra
